After 15 long days in the Atlantic Ocean, we have finally reached the most remote settlement on Earth, Tristan da Cunha.

We’re in the middle of the ocean, between South America and Africa. Right here, there’s a tiny island you can barely see on the map. The nearest settlement is thousands of kilometers away from here. So in this entire vast area, no one lives except the people of Tristan.

For centuries, the loneliest people on Earth have lived an unusual life here. Their population is just 222.

There is not an airport on Tristan da Cunha. The only way to reach the island, or to leave it, is a very long sea voyage on one of the few ships that make the trip.

So, how aware are these people of what’s happening in the world? What does it feel like to live in the middle of nowhere?
